title: Systematic token smoothing and shadow clarity for high-contrast rows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We will introduce a smoothing layer for design tokens and a clarified elevation/penumbra system focused on high-contrast row scenarios (data tables, dense lists, and compact controls). The goal is to reduce visual jitter across density modes, improve perceived contrast for hover/focus states, and provide an explicit mapping for button/table elevation tokens that engineers can adopt without bespoke overrides.

Context: Multiple components (tables, buttons, action rows) are currently relying on point values for elevation and neutral ramps that produce visible stepping when density toggles or when chroma is tuned for dark/high-contrast modes. This ticket synthesizes work from the token audit (DES-314159) and accessibility feedback to produce a deterministic interpolation strategy and a small set of canonical elevation tokens (z-steps) with penumbra taper profiles.

Goals:
- Define a token smoothing function and alias mapping so existing tokens migrate without breaking components.
- Introduce 4 canonical elevation tokens (z-0, z-1, z-2, z-3) with detailed shadow layering (ambient + penumbra + contact) and a penumbra taper curve parameter.
- Add density-aware typography deltas for dense tables: reduce body-small from 13px to 12px for compact mode, adjust line-height accordingly, and verify legibility at 3:1 contrast for supplementary text.
- Establish spacing/radius interpolation rules (0.5px steps for compact mode, proportional radii for pills/controls).
- Provide codemods and token alias table for the engineering team to migrate components in a single sprint.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma spec sheet with interpolation previews for Light/Dark/High-Contrast variants uploaded and approved by design lead.
- Token JSON export (semantic tokens) with aliases and migration notes checked into tokens repo (PR linked).
- Engineering PRs for Button and Table consume new z-steps and pass visual regression tests (percy) with no >2px layout shifts.
- Accessibility QA confirms body-small at compact density meets minimum readable size target and that elevation contrast does not reduce text contrast below 4.5:1 for interactive labels.

Trade-offs considered:
- We intentionally limit the canonical elevation set to 4 steps to avoid combinatorial token explosion; this requires small visual compromises in very custom components, which will be addressed by providing escape tokens (explicit overrides) with added review gating.
- Smoothing reduces abrupt color/elevation jumps but slightly blurs the mental model of exact pixel-perfect layering; we compensate by publishing visual regression thresholds and design guidelines.

Migration plan:
1) Publish token specification and alias table. 2) Land tokens JSON in tokens repo and create codemods for common component patterns (buttons, table-rows, badges). 3) Engineering picks up codemods and targets one component per PR. 4) QA runs visual diffs and accessibility checks. 5) Rollout toggled behind feature-flag for 2 weeks before full switch.

Notes & links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Token-Smoothing-2026 (spec page: "z-steps + penumbra")
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.internal.redwood.ai/display/DES/Token+Smoothing+and+Shadow+Clarity
- Tokens repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokens/pull/482
- Dev codemod branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend-codemods/tree/des-84763

Longer-term considerations: Evaluate whether the penumbra taper parameter can be exposed in Redwood Optimize tooling to suggest token profiles per workload (e.g., compact/dense analytics vs. admin panels).
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Design, Eng (Marco, Priya), and PM (Sofia). Aligned on scope: tokens + two components (Button, Table).

2026-02-20: Prototype in Figma demonstrates smoother transitions between neutral-300 and neutral-400 across density toggles. Asked Eng to try dev proof-of-concept with CSS variables and layered shadows.
2026-02-26: Engineering spike (ENG-20984) implemented penumbra taper via dual-shadow approach; early perf checks show negligible repaint cost. Shared demo PR link in attachments.
2026-03-03: Design review with accessibility team. Adjusted body-small scale and added extra contrast testcases for hover/active states. Updated spec.
2026-03-08: Codemod initial pass created for primary button patterns; running codemod on /packages/button. Found 6 custom overrides that require manual review.
2026-03-10: Scoped QA run scheduled for 2026-03-15; feature flag prepared for canary rollout.
